Learn to explain how to stop async work that is no longer needed: Task Cancellation, CancellationError & Cancellation Handler, with real code, a quiz at the end and each example read twice (normal, then slow).

Today's terms
Task Cancellation - A request that tells a task to stop its work as soon as it can.
CancellationError - An error that Swift throws to show that a task was cancelled.
Cancellation Handler - A closure that runs right away when a task is cancelled, even while the task is waiting.

landscape.hook: Can you explain Task Cancellation, CancellationError and Cancellation Handler in English?

dialogue.title: The search that never stops
dialogue.setting: A task that keeps running after the screen closes

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Jake, my search screen keeps loading after the user leaves it.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: You need task cancellation. When the screen closes, call `task.cancel()`.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: I did, but the loop still runs to the end.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Task cancellation is only a request. Your code must check it.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Call `Task.checkCancellation()`. It throws a CancellationError when the task was cancelled.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: So CancellationError is not a real failure?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Right. It only shows that the task was cancelled, so catch it and stop quietly.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: What if the task waits on a network call?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Use a cancellation handler. A cancellation handler runs right away when the task is cancelled, even while it waits.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: That sounds useful for closing connections.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Yes. Task cancellation plus a cancellation handler keeps the app clean.
Task cancellation tells the work to stop.
